analyst_view.overall: Early view: a big chance for Salzburg, who are unbeaten and second in the Austrian league but 26th in Europe with one win in four. Bottom side Ararat-Armenia (0 points, 14 goals conceded) are without goalkeeper Joao Bravim, sent off at Torreense, and defender Bruno Wilson, banned after three yellow cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. I lean higher: Ararat have conceded 14 in four games and now have to change goalkeeper, while Salzburg have won eight and drawn three in the Austrian league. Salzburg's European scoring (three goals in four) is the one worry, but Ararat have scored in three of four, which adds to the total.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. I lean a little higher: Salzburg should have long spells of possession against the competition's leakiest defence, and a stand-in keeper and a reshuffled back line tend to clear rather than claim, which feeds corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean a little higher: Ararat arrive with one player sent off and another banned for accumulated yellows, a sign of a side that has been picking up cards while chasing games, and they are likely to be chasing again in Salzburg.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots. Salzburg should dominate and Ararat's games have been open (18 goals in four), so a high total fits; I see no reason to move away from it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Ararat concede plenty of chances, but Salzburg have scored only twice in their last three European games, including 0-2 at Anderlecht, so I would not go above the number.
